core/recipe_fix.py - user-friendly recipe repair (no regex knowledge needed).

Two helpers back the new "confirm the RESULT, not the recipe" dialog:

* ``synth_anchor_for_value(doc_lines, value)``
    Given a value the user typed (e.g. ``PO10151999``), find the line in the
    source PDF that contains it and build a regex anchor that captures exactly
    that value, swallowing the label/colon. So an ordinary office worker never
    writes a regex - they only type the correct text.

* ``sanitize_recipe_anchors(recipe, doc_lines)``
    Auto-fixes the most common AI mistakes BEFORE the dialog is shown:
      1. a captured value that still carries a leading colon (``:PO10151999``)
         -> re-synthesize the anchor so it captures cleanly;
      2. ``UNIT PRICE`` without Turkish dotted-I tolerance -> ``UNIT PR[İI]CE``;
      3. a price anchor that fails to match at all -> fall back to the known-good
         default shape.
    This makes the preview correct by default, so the confirm step is usually a
    single click.

Turn a raw label (e.g. ``ORDER NO....:``) into a relaxed regex piece.

    Dots -> ``\.+``, whitespace -> ``\s+``, regex-special chars escaped,
    everything else kept verbatim (so a Turkish dotted-I label still matches).

Build an anchor regex that captures ``value`` from the source lines.

    Returns the regex string, or ``None`` if ``value`` cannot be located / the
    generated pattern fails to compile.

If ``removed`` is a sequence of hyphen-separated alphanumeric tokens,
    return a structural regex that strips the same *shape* of suffix/prefix
    instead of a literal string. This lets one correction (e.g.
    ``"014KK-08X-XS"`` -> ``"014KK"``) clean sibling styles like
    ``"257FM-09Y-S"`` or ``"637JO-10Z-M"`` without learning each suffix.

    ``side`` is "tail" (orig starts with new, removed is at the end) or
    "head" (orig ends with new, removed is at the beginning).
    Returns ``{"pat", "repl"}`` or ``None``.

From a user correction (orig -> new), build a regex-sub spec that yields
    ``new`` given ``orig`` and generalises to sibling values of the same layout.

    Strategy (most specific first):
      * new is a prefix of orig -> strip the trailing removed chunk. E.g.
        ``"014KK-08X-XS"`` -> ``"014KK"`` yields a structural rule that strips
        the trailing ``-COLOR-SIZE`` tokens, so ``"257FM-09Y-S"`` also cleans
        to ``"257FM"`` on later POs.
      * new is a suffix of orig -> strip the leading removed chunk.
      * otherwise -> literal replace ``orig`` -> ``new`` (constant field,
        e.g. a fixed color that never varies across POs).
    Returns ``{"pat", "repl"}`` or ``None`` when the correction is degenerate
    (empty / unchanged).

Cleanup-transform for the combined "CODE / DESC" color string.

    Two *structural* branches (each fixes EVERY color group of the layout with a
    single edit), tried in order, then a literal fallback:

    1. **Full strip** – the user keeps only the DESC segment after " / "
       (``"08X / SAND"`` -> ``"SAND"``). Everything up to and including the first
       " / " is removed. The color_code column becomes empty. Use this only when
       the code carries no disambiguating value.

    2. **Repeat-code strip (A-2, keeps color_code)** – the raw combined string
       embeds a *repeated* code token in front of the real color name, e.g.
       ``"08X / TROUSERS 08X 08X SAND"``. The user trims the box down to the pure
       color name (``"SAND"``, or equivalently ``"08X / SAND"``). We then derive a
       rule that removes the middle noise **up to and including the doubled
       token** while PRESERVING the leading ``code / `` prefix, so ``color_code``
       - and therefore ``_Row Key`` - stays distinguishable between colors that
       share one PO. Lazy ``.*?`` is mandatory: a greedy ``.*`` would latch onto
       the *last* doubled token and eat into adversarial names such as
       ``"OFF OFF WHITE"``.

    Falls back to :func:`derive_clean_transform` (literal, non-propagating) when
    neither structural shape is recognised.

Append a cleanup rule to ``recipe.cleans[field]`` (no overwrite).

    ``rule`` format:
        * regex: ``{"pat": "...", "repl": "..."}``  (existing behaviour)
        * normalizer: ``{"type": "normalize_date"}``  (V2.0.19.10+)
        * normalizer with params: ``{"type": "normalize_term", "vocab": {...}}``

    Duplicate rules are skipped (idempotent).  ``pat``-based rules are deduped
    on ``(pat, repl)``; ``type``-based rules are deduped on ``(type, vocab)``.
    A rule with neither ``pat`` nor ``type`` is ignored.
Repair obvious AI anchor bugs against the real document. Returns recipe.
